description: Gripper Gen 12: tweezer version that follows the fingers. Jake (voice): 'Do another version. It should be basically a set of tweezers that can follow the fingers. Pretty similar to what we have now, but significantly smaller at the end, and more tweezer-like.' Start from the current Generalist-style fingers (Gen 10/11) and keep the same family look and mounting/pivot idea, but make it a tweezer: the jaws track the wearer's thumb and index finger motion; the fingers taper to much smaller, finer, flatter tweezer tips for precise small-object picks; the tips meet cleanly when closed. New version only; don't modify earlier generations. Include it in the gallery with the open/close slider. (Separately, notes from the Gen 10 vs 11 comparison for future Generalist-copy versions: shallow grooves only on the gripping jaw near the tip, not along the whole edge; Gen 10's fuller beak looked closer than Gen 11's needle.)

results.notes: Correction to the side note in the description: Jake now says the serration DOES span essentially the entire inner edge (except maybe the very tip), per the closed reference photo. Ignore 'grooves only near the tip'. .

results.identified_issue: Built in SCAD, not in trace_photo.py: profile() is now Gen 11's traced outline below z=80, intersected beyond that with tine_envelope (outer edge tine_out(z) = land_x+tip_w+(-13-land_x-tip_w)(1-f)^1.6), plus a straight land strip x=land_x for z 96..tip, clipped to x>=land_x so nothing reaches past the meeting plane. tip_gap=0 makes the lands coplanar at angle 0. OpenSCAD then returns a ~1e-9 mm sliver for clash(0), so check_geometry treats an X-extent under 1 µm as touch-only and samples collisions from 1° up. half_thick changed from 1-f^2 to (1-f)^1.5 with tip_thick 2.4. ridges_px is still generated in trace_px.scad but unused; ridges2d cuts its own land grooves. genus.py now asks OpenSCAD for len(slots_kept). Scripts/publish_designs.py (untracked, not committed, someone else's local file) got a generations entry 'v012-generalist-tweezer': 12 so it's named 'Gen 12'; without it the gallery shows the folder name. VERSIONS.txt (untracked) got a line, also not committed. I regenerated Gen 11's ignored exports/*.stl because publish_designs falls back to a single fused mesh when the exports are older than the .scad, which broke test_gripper_poses for v011. Alternatives not taken: lengthening the tine, or 11b's chisel beak as the base.
results.summary: Gen 12 tweezer is in the gallery: Gen 11's fingers with slender tines and flat 1.4 mm tips that meet along an 11 mm land
results.detailed_description: Gen 12 starts from Gen 11 r4 (Gen 10's beak, jaw-only grooves) and keeps its root unchanged: the honeycomb, hook lip, black dot, pivot frame and 0–30° swing. So the pair follows thumb and index the same way. Past the black dot, each blade becomes a tweezer tine. The outer edge tapers to a 1.4 mm tip (~11 mm across at the dot; ~3 mm at 7 mm from the tip, ~1.8 mm at 3 mm). The jaw edge runs dead straight over the last ~11 mm. At closed (0°) the two straight edges close flat against each other along that whole length, where Gen 11 left a 1 mm gap between points. The blade also thins in thickness and levels off, so the end is a flat 2.4 × 1.4 mm pad instead of a beak point. The reach stays the same, ~107 mm. Following your Gen 10 vs 11 note, the grooves are now only 7 shallow cross-cuts (0.3 mm deep) on the gripping edge, 1–6 mm back from the tip. Things you'd notice: Gen 11's last 3 blade slots don't fit in the slender tine, so they're gone (30 through-holes instead of 33), and the pivot spacing moves from ±27.67 to ±27.1 mm to make the tips meet. Checks: watertight single-body STLs; the hole count matches the design; no collision from 1 to 30°; at 0° the tips touch with no overlap, and pushing them 0.05 mm together overlaps along the tip region. The gallery shows it as Gen 12 with the open/close slider; I added a poses.js entry. Also: the gallery had been showing Gen 11 as one fused mesh with no working slider, because its .stl exports were 28 s older than its .scad. I re-exported those (git-ignored) STLs from the unchanged source, and Gen 11 opens and closes again. Not verified: the scale is still the assumed 0.2 mm/px, there's no mount or spring, and a 1.4 mm PLA tine will flex (fine for tweezers, but untested).
results.user_reply_draft: Hey Jake — Gen 12 is up in the gallery. It's the Gen 11 fingers turned into tweezers. Everything from the dot back stays the same, so it moves with your fingers like before. Past the dot, each finger slims down to a thin, flat 1.4 mm tip. When you close it, the two tips press flat against each other along the last centimetre, instead of stopping short like Gen 11 did. There are just a few fine grooves right at the tip for grip. Slide it open and shut and tell me if the tips should go even finer or longer.

summary: Gen 12 is a new tweezer-style version of the Generalist fingers, with slender tines and small flat tips, shown in the gallery with the open/close slider. Serration should span nearly the whole inner edge, except maybe the very tip, replacing the earlier "grooves only near the tip" note.
